text.p: SubMicron Systems Corp, which supplies advanced wafer processing equipment to the semiconductor industry, said on Monday it was reorganizing its operations to deal with a slowdown in the industry.

"The current slowdown in our industry has created a need to reduce costs, and customers are requiring performance standards beyond any previous level," David Levy, chairman and chief executive officer, said.
The company said it was centralizing sales and service activities, bundling product offerings and looking to expand its turnkey and systems integration participation.
Each subsidiary would focus on operating results while meeting customer requirements, the company said.
"SubMicron Systems is responding to the challenge by restructuring in such a way as to create the most benefit to the customer while providing for the interests of our shareholders," Levy said.
The company said it named James Molinaro senior vice president, with a focus on worldwide sales and services.

Norman Jones and Wendell Windell were named to the newly created posts of vice president, general manager, and vice president, plant manager, respectively, at its Systems Chemistry unit, SubMicron said.
They would focus on product direction and daily operations and efficiencies, the company said.

"Subsidiary and administrative organizational realignment and reassignments are part of a continual improvement process, to which we are committed," Levy said. "We are comfortable that this will provide significant results as we move forward."
